description:
The permanent-campaign runner executes its whole pipeline as one uninterrupted overnight session; converge it on @/inv/campaign-resumability so completed cells persist as checkpointed evidence and an interrupted, censored, or budget-exhausted run continues without repeating completed work.

## Background

Registered invariant @/inv/campaign-resumability post-dates the runner (dev/scripts/permanent-campaign-runner.sh) and the permanent-sampling-feas harness. The harness's disjoint per-cell stream addressing already makes every cell independently reproducible, so cell-granular checkpointing is a scheduling concern, not a sampling redesign. Cost of the status quo: the e31b1918 harness fix forced regenerating all three fields' evidence in one ~2.3 h night even though only the equivalence step changed.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A measure run records per-cell completion durably; re-invoking the runner after an interruption or budget stop executes only cells without committed evidence and produces a dataset identical to an uninterrupted run (deterministic-seeded-execution holds across the resume boundary).
- [hard] REQ-02: A run can be budget-bounded (wall-clock or cell count) and exits cleanly at the bound with a resumable state and an explicit run-summary status.
- [hard] REQ-03: Runner tests cover interrupt-and-resume and budget-stop-and-resume paths.

## Notes

Enforces @/inv/campaign-resumability. Coordinate with 3ea21d74 and 79c5ace7 (harness output-schema fixes) so schema and scheduling changes land in one tool revision where practical.
title: Resumable multi-night execution for the campaign runner
